tfn.s: Ticketmaster agreed to explain prices more clearly after action by the UK's competition authority.
tfn.why: The text says: "The UK's competition authority later made Ticketmaster agree to explain prices more clearly."

tfn.s: Resale websites always sell tickets at the original price.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "Resale websites sometimes show tickets at much higher prices than the original cost."

tfn.s: Ticket prices have risen faster in Britain than elsewhere.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not compare ticket prices in Britain with other countries.

tfn.s: Some concerts have several different price levels.
tfn.why: The text says: "Some concerts have several price levels."

tfn.s: Oasis fans knew before the sale that standing tickets had different prices.
tfn.why: The text says fans waited "without realising that standing tickets were being sold at different fixed prices".

focus.note: Some words just go together. We say a long queue and take part, but not a tall queue or join part.

tfn.s: The authority was unhappy mainly about how the ticket tiers were presented, not about prices changing in real time.
tfn.why: Its concerns "centred on the way different ticket tiers and their benefits were presented", and it found no evidence of real-time dynamic pricing.

tfn.s: The text says streaming pays musicians about the same as album sales once did.
tfn.why: The income from streaming is described as "very different from the old business of selling physical albums".

tfn.s: Small independent venues offer cheaper live music, but many find it hard to survive.
tfn.why: The text says they offer "much cheaper live music, though many struggle to stay open".

tfn.s: Ticketmaster has since changed how its website shows ticket tiers.
tfn.why: The text says it gave commitments, but not whether it has made changes yet.

tfn.s: The authority decided that the Oasis sale used dynamic pricing but approved of it.
tfn.why: It "did not find evidence" of real-time dynamic pricing in the Oasis sale.

focus.note: Learn the verb with its noun as one unit. We make a decision and have no choice, but we do not do a decision.

tfn.s: The authority's findings suggest that the Oasis sale's difficulties came from poor communication rather than algorithmic pricing.
tfn.why: It found that Ticketmaster "had not communicated key information adequately" but did not establish real-time price fluctuations.

tfn.s: The writer says the Oasis sale proved that dynamic pricing was used.
tfn.why: The authority "did not establish" real-time algorithmic price fluctuations.

tfn.s: The writer believes clearer pricing information would make concerts affordable.
tfn.why: The text says "Transparency is not the same thing as affordability".

tfn.s: The authority ordered Ticketmaster to refund fans who bought tiered tickets.
tfn.why: Refunds are never mentioned; the text only describes undertakings about information.

tfn.s: Independent venues face pressure whichever side of the pricing argument is accepted.
tfn.why: "Neither argument removes the pressure on independent venues."

speak.title: Role-play: is the ticket worth it?
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.role: the friend who wants to go
a.text: Your favourite singer is on tour and tickets are very expensive. You want to buy two. Explain why it matters to you. Ask your friend to come, and answer their worries.

b.role: the friend who is not sure
b.text: You like the singer, but the ticket, the travel and a hotel cost a lot. Ask questions about the total price. Suggest another plan, then decide together.

phrases: I'd love to go, but it's a lot of money.
It's a once in a lifetime chance.
How much would it cost in total?
We could save up for it.
What about a smaller gig instead?
I think it's worth it, don't you?
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did you buy the tickets, and was it a fair decision?
